subject: Attribution & CLA negotiation with Aurora Models
messages:
From: sergio alvarez <sergio@redwood.com>
To: Elena Petrov <elena@auroramodels.ai>
Cc: camila reyes <camila@redwood.com>, karthik iyer <karthik@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 25 Feb 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Attribution & CLA discussion — Aurora models distribution

Hi Elena — great to meet over the call last week. Thanks for sending the initial outline.

We'd like to move quickly on a partner CLA so we can onboard Aurora models into Redwood's partner catalog and offer a mirrored hosting option for enterprise customers. A few items we need to align on before legal exchange:

- Attribution: how must Aurora be credited in API responses and UI? We usually include a short-model badge and a per-response attribution string; need to know if that satisfies your marketing/visibility requirements.
- Redistribution / mirrors: Redwood supports partner-hosted mirrors (dedicated pools for partners) and customer-hosted variants. Can Aurora permit mirror hosting under a partner tier if mirrors are limited to enterprise partners and not public CDN mirrors?
- Weights access: do you allow customers to download raw weights under any tier? If so, what controls (embargo periods, vetting) do you require?
- Telemetry & audit: Aurora asked for usage telemetry & model fingerprinting — we can provide aggregated calls and token counts plus signed request log access for audits. Need to agree on frequency & retention.

Attached: brief Redwood attribution guidelines and a sample MPA clause set (redwood_attribution_guidelines.md). If you could share Aurora_CLA_Draft, we can mark redlines and loop in legal.

Proposed next step: quick legal sync Thu or Fri, otherwise we can exchange redlines via DocuSign.

Thanks,
Sergio Alvarez
Enterprise Partnerships, Redwood Inference
sergio@redwood.com

Attachments: redwood_attribution_guidelines.md (text), sample_mpa_clause.txt (text)
From: Elena Petrov <elena@auroramodels.ai>
To: sergio alvarez <sergio@redwood.com>
Cc: Aurora Models Legal <legal@auroramodels.ai>
Date: Thu, 26 Feb 2026 11:04:00 -0500
Subject: Re: Attribution & CLA discussion — Aurora models distribution

Hi Sergio — thanks for the clear summary. Attaching Aurora_CLA_Draft_v3.pdf with our current preferred language. High-level answers: 

- Attribution: We require a visible attribution line ("Model: Aurora-Lite v2 — Aurora Models") in the UI for non-API bulk-download use. For API responses, a per-response attribution token is sufficient (we provide exact phrasing in the CLA). No co-branding beyond that without marketing approvals.
- Mirrors: We allow partner mirrors on a case-by-case basis. Mirrors must be access-controlled (no public anonymous access) and only permitted for paying enterprise customers listed in Schedule A.
- Weights: We do not allow unrestricted download of raw full-precision weights in the standard partner tier. A vetted "research" tier can allow weight sharing under an additional agreement and embargo.
- Telemetry: Aggregated usage (tokens, request rates) is fine. For audit requests we can provide verification artifacts on a quarterly cadence. No raw request payloads unless court/order or a separate agreement is in place.

We'll have legal propose precise redline language; see attached. If Redwood can accept a clause that restricts public redistribution and enforces schedule-based mirror lists, we're comfortable moving forward.

Best,
Elena Petrov
Head of Partnerships, Aurora Models
elena@auroramodels.ai

Attachment: Aurora_CLA_Draft_v3.pdf (pdf - 412KB)
From: camila reyes <camila@redwood.com>
To: Elena Petrov <elena@auroramodels.ai>
Cc: sergio alvarez <sergio@redwood.com>, karthik iyer <karthik@redwood.com>, marissa cole <marissa@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 27 Feb 2026 08:27:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Attribution & CLA discussion — Aurora models distribution

Hi Elena — thanks for the draft and the clear replies. Quick internal notes and proposed redlines attached. Main negotiation points from our side: 

1) Attribution: We can adopt the short attribution token in API responses. Suggest an option to place a badge in the Redwood Console under "Model Details" with a link to Aurora's model page — this is non-marketing placement and respects your no co-branding ask.

2) Mirrors: Redwood requests the ability to host "partner mirrors" to improve latency for enterprise customers in regions where Aurora has limited presence. Proposed constraint: mirrors are access-restricted and appear in Schedule A as you requested; we also propose an automated sync-check (SHA verification) to confirm integrity.

3) Weights access: We agree to limit raw weights in the standard partner tier. We propose a technical workflow for the research tier: Aurora signs off on a short vetting questionnaire + mutual NDA and we host ephemeral, time-limited access rather than a full public download.

4) Telemetry & Audit: Redwood will provide aggregated usage dashboards and quarterly audit exports (signed manifests). For any legal-level forensic requests, we'll route through Redwood's CS and your legal team.

Attached redlines: "redwood_marketing_attribution_redlines.md" and a proposed Schedule A template.

If this looks OK, we can prepare a single redline doc and route via DocuSign. Would prefer to keep SLA/price negotiations separate from the CLA signature if possible (we can tie pricing into a separate partner addendum).

Cheers,
Camila Reyes
Head of Partner Programs, Redwood Inference
camila@redwood.com

Attachments: redwood_marketing_attribution_redlines.md, scheduleA_template.xlsx
From: karthik iyer <karthik@redwood.com>
To: Elena Petrov <elena@auroramodels.ai>, camila reyes <camila@redwood.com>, sergio alvarez <sergio@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 01 Mar 2026 10:16:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Attribution & CLA discussion — technical + hosting constraints

Elena / team — looping in technical constraints and proposed guardrails from Redwood infra: 

- Mirror hosting: We can offer two mirror modes: 
  a) Partner-Hosted (private customer bundles) — mirrors are within Redwood's partner pool, access controlled via tenant mapping. No anonymous endpoints.
  b) Enterprise Mirror (on-prem/cloud region) — dedicated to a single enterprise customer; requires Schedule A entry.

- Integrity & verification: We propose SHA256 manifest signed by Aurora for any mirrored snapshot. Redwood will verify signature before serving and will surface drift alerts if hashes diverge.

- Weight formats & quantization: To avoid unrestricted full-precision weight exposure, Redwood can host quantized runtime artifacts (INT8/4bit) for runtime inference. Raw FP32/FP16 exports will be available only under Research Tier (vetting + additional controls).

- Audit logs & telemetry: Redwood can provide token-level aggregated counts and per-deployment telemetry feeds for customers. For Aurora audits we can provide signed manifests and per-deployment consumption summaries monthly. Full request payloads are never stored by default; we propose a mutual process for any exceptional forensic request.

One ask from our side: if Aurora requires model watermarking/fingerprinting to enforce downstream policy, we need a short spec for how fingerprinting will be validated on hosted inference vs customer-hosted variants.

Happy to run a short tech demo of the mirror and verification flow if that helps accelerate the CLA attachment.

Thanks,
Karthik Iyer
VP, Platform Engineering, Redwood Inference
karthik@redwood.com
From: Aurora Models Legal <legal@auroramodels.ai>
To: camila reyes <camila@redwood.com>, sergio alvarez <sergio@redwood.com>, karthik iyer <karthik@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 02 Mar 2026 16:03:00 -0500
Subject: Re: Attribution & CLA discussion — final redlines and signature

Camila / team — thanks for the thoughtful redlines. Our legal reviewed Karthik's technical proposals and we are comfortable with the partner-hosted mirror model and the signed manifest verification approach. A few final items: 

- We tightened the weights access language to explicitly disallow "public redistribution" and to require Schedule A listing for any mirrors.
- We added a short clause that allows Aurora to request a compliance review (quarterly) with 30 days' notice — Redwood's obligation will be to provide signed manifests and aggregated logs only.
- We accepted your proposal to keep pricing/SLA in a separate addendum.

We're prepared to sign pending acceptance of two small edits (clarify attribution phrase and add a short definition for "Research Tier"). I've uploaded the redlined CLA to DocuSign: https://www.docusign.com/en/signing/AAA-aurora-cla (expires in 7 days). Please sign and we will countersign.

Proposed next step: sign DocuSign and schedule an ops/tech onboarding on 10 Mar (30 minutes).

Regards,
Aurora Models Legal
legal@auroramodels.ai

Attachment: Aurora_CLA_Draft_v3_redlined.pdf (pdf)
